title: Number of Restricted Paths From First to Last Node
summary: Given an undirected weighted connected graph with n nodes labeled from 1 to n, and an array of edges where each edge connects two nodes with a specific weight, calculate the number of restricted paths from node 1 to node n.
statement: Given an undirected weighted connected graph with n nodes labeled from 1 to n, and an array of edges where each edge connects two nodes with a specific weight, calculate the number of restricted paths from node 1 to node n. A restricted path is defined as a path where the distance to the last node strictly decreases at each step. The result should be returned modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: The graph is connected, undirected, weighted, and uses node labels 1 through n.
A restricted path must strictly decrease the shortest distance to node n at every step; return its count modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: First compute every node’s shortest distance to node n.
Dijkstra from n gives those distances; they orient every valid step into a decreasing-distance DAG.
Process nodes from smaller to larger distance and propagate path counts to larger-distance neighbors.
Every restricted path follows the distance order, so dynamic programming counts each path once after Dijkstra fixes the ordering.
editorial: Every restricted path follows the distance order, so dynamic programming counts each path once after Dijkstra fixes the ordering.

tests.explanation: Only 1-3-7 decreases the shortest remaining distance at both steps.
